newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile copper mines hit by power cuts - El Abra.
newsitem.headline: Chile copper mines hit by power cuts - El Abra.

text.p: Two power cuts in the last 24 hours caused by rain and high winds in northern Chile have created production problems for copper mines in the region, said a top official at the El Abra pit.

The recently opened El Abra mine lost electricity for an hour Sunday and received limited power for six hours Monday morning as a result of the outages on the northern grid, John Fenn, vice president of operations, told Reuters by telephone from Calama.
"The outage did cause a halt in production...Every time we shut down, we lose two to three hours of production," he said.

Fenn said he believed the electricity problems also hit other large producers in the area supplied by the grid which include state-owned Codelco's Chuquicamata pit, Escondida and the smaller Zaldivar mine.
Officials from these mines were not available for comment.
El Abra, which came on line last year, produces 617 tonnes of cathodes a day and the power cuts may have cost the company production of 100 tonnes of cathodes, he said.
"The potential loss is 100 tonnes as you can't plate (cathodes) if you have outages," he said. "But some of this can be made up."
During periods of restricted power, the mine keeps vital areas such as the cathodes tankhouse running but cuts electricity to less crucial operations, he said.
The mine is 51 percent owned by Cyprus Amax Minerals with the rest owned by Codelco.
The northern grid, which supplies power to most of Chile's all-important copper mining industry, has been plagued with problems in recent months.
These weekend's outages are the most serious since a day-long power cut in December.
The grid, which includes at least three large power producers, has come under increasing strain as the result of the rapid growth of the mining industry.
